questions.question: You’re waiting in line at the café when your friend’s order is called before yours. What would be the most polite way to respond?
options: I’ll just wait here—thanks!
You’re so lucky! I was about to ask for the same thing.
I’ll go grab my coffee now. Thanks for nothing!
Oh, that’s great! Maybe I’ll join you.

questions.question: Your colleague says, *'We could really use more volunteers for the charity event this weekend. Anyone interested?'* How would you politely respond if you’re not available but could help another time?
options: That’s a great idea! I’ll definitely help next time.
I’m sorry, I can’t make it this time, but I’m happy to help in the future.
Volunteering? Never heard of it—what’s the point?
You’re on! I’ll be there at 10 AM.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, I can’t make it this time, but I’m happy to help in the future.

questions.question: Your friend asks, *'Do you think it’s okay to wear jeans to work on Fridays?'* You’re unsure but generally agree with casual Fridays. What would be the most appropriate response?
options: Absolutely not! That’s not professional at all.
Well, it depends—some offices are very strict about dress codes.
I’d say yes, but only if they’re clean and well-fitted.
I don’t know, but I think jeans are fine as long as you look neat.
questions.answer: Well, it depends—some offices are very strict about dress codes.

questions.question: You’re at a party and someone asks, *'Have you tried the new restaurant downtown? It’s amazing!'* You’ve never been before. What would be the best way to respond if you’re curious but not ready to commit?
options: Really? I’ve heard good things about it—let’s go there next weekend!
I’ve never been, but I’d love to hear more about it—thanks for the tip!
That sounds terrible. I’ll stick to my usual place.
I’m not interested. I’ve got plans tonight.
questions.answer: I’ve never been, but I’d love to hear more about it—thanks for the tip!

questions.question: Your boss says to you, *'I’m afraid we won’t be able to meet your deadline this time. Can we discuss alternatives?'* How would you respond if you’re concerned but want to show professionalism?
options: Great! Let’s figure out a new plan right away.
That’s fine—I’ll work on it tomorrow.
I don’t think that’s a good idea. We should stick to the original schedule.
I’m sorry to hear that. Could we look at ways to adjust the timeline?
questions.answer: I’m sorry to hear that. Could we look at ways to adjust the timeline?
